nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language. The accepting Nerode classes of $L$ are those whose words belong to $L$: the Nerode class $[x]$ of a word $x$ is accepting if and only if $x \in L$. This is well-defined because Nerode equivalent words are either both in $L$ or both outside $L$.
nodes.title: Accepting Nerode classes

nodes.summary: For every language $L$, the language accepted by the Nerode automaton of $L$ is exactly $L$.
nodes.title: The Nerode automaton recognizes its language

nodes.summary: A DFA is accessible when every state is reachable.
nodes.title: Accessible DFA

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with finitely many Nerode classes, and let $M$ be a DFA with a finite set of states $Q$ that accepts exactly $L$. Send each Nerode class of $L$ to the state that $M$ reaches from its start state on the chosen representative word of the class. Then the number of Nerode classes of $L$ equals $|Q|$ if and only if every state in $Q$ is the image of some Nerode class under this map.
nodes.title: Equality case of the Nerode state bound

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with finitely many Nerode classes, and let $M$ be a DFA with a finite set of states $Q$ that accepts exactly $L$. Then the number of Nerode classes of $L$ is at most $|Q|$.
nodes.title: Nerode classes bound the number of DFA states

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with finitely many Nerode classes, and let $M$ be a DFA with a finite set of states $Q$ that accepts exactly $L$. Send each Nerode class of $L$ to the state that $M$ reaches from its start state on the chosen representative word of the class. If some state in $Q$ is not the image of any Nerode class under this map, then the number of Nerode classes of $L$ is strictly less than $|Q|$.
nodes.title: Strict Nerode state bound

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language. The residual map sends the Nerode class $[x]$ of a word $x$ to the left quotient $x^{-1}L = \{ y \mid xy \in L \}$, viewed as an element of the set $\{ w^{-1}L \mid w \text{ a word} \}$ of left quotients of $L$. It is well-defined because Nerode equivalent words have the same left quotient.
nodes.title: Residual map on Nerode classes

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$. Two words $x$ and $y$ over $\Sigma$ are distinguishable by $L$ when there is a word $z$ over $\Sigma$ such that exactly one of $xz$ and $yz$ belongs to $L$.
nodes.title: Distinguishable words

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language and let $M$ be a DFA that accepts exactly $L$. If two words $x$ and $y$ are distinguishable by $L$, then the states that $M$ reaches from its start state on reading $x$ and on reading $y$ are different.
nodes.title: Distinguishable words reach different DFA states

nodes.summary: For every language $L$, writing $x^{-1}L = \{ y \mid xy \in L \}$ for the left quotient of $L$ by a word $x$, there are finitely many Nerode classes of $L$ if and only if the set $\{ x^{-1}L \mid x \text{ a word} \}$ of left quotients of $L$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finitely many Nerode classes iff finitely many left quotients

nodes.summary: A language $L$ is regular, that is, accepted by some deterministic finite automaton, if and only if $L$ has finitely many Nerode classes.
nodes.title: Myhill–Nerode theorem, quotient form

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language. If two words $x$ and $y$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$, then $x \in L$ if and only if $y \in L$.
nodes.title: Nerode equivalent words agree on membership

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language and let $M$ be a DFA with a finite set of states $Q$ that accepts exactly $L$. For a word $x$, the left quotient of $L$ by $x$ is the language $\{z \mid xz \in L\}$. Then the number of distinct left quotients of $L$ is at most $|Q|$.
nodes.title: Myhill–Nerode lower bound via left quotients

nodes.summary: For a language $L$ and a word $x$, the Nerode class $[x]$ of $x$ is the equivalence class of $x$ under Nerode equivalence for $L$.
nodes.title: Nerode class of a word

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language and let $M$ be a DFA that accepts exactly $L$. This is the bijection from the Nerode classes of $L$ to the reachable residuals of $M$, the languages accepted by $M$ from states it reaches from its start state. It sends the Nerode class of a word $x$ to the left quotient $\{z \mid xz \in L\}$, which is the language $M$ accepts from the state it reaches on reading $x$.
nodes.title: Nerode classes correspond to reachable residuals

nodes.summary: For every language $L$, the map sending the Nerode class $[x]$ of a word $x$ to the left quotient $x^{-1}L = \{ y \mid xy \in L \}$ is a bijection from the set of Nerode classes of $L$ onto the set $\{ w^{-1}L \mid w \text{ a word} \}$ of left quotients of $L$.
nodes.title: Bijection between Nerode classes and left quotients

nodes.summary: For a language $L$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$, the Nerode classes of $L$ are the elements of the quotient of the set of words over $\Sigma$ by Nerode equivalence for $L$, under which two words $x$ and $y$ are equivalent when they have the same left quotient, that is, when for every word $z$ we have $xz \in L$ if and only if $yz \in L$.
nodes.title: Nerode classes

nodes.summary: For every language $L$ and every Nerode class $q$ of $L$, there is a word $x$ such that the Nerode automaton of $L$, started in its start state and reading $x$, ends in the state $q$.
nodes.title: Every state of the Nerode automaton is reachable

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$. The Nerode automaton of $L$ is the deterministic automaton over $\Sigma$, not necessarily finite, whose states are the Nerode classes of words for $L$, whose start state is the class of the empty word, which on reading a symbol $a \in \Sigma$ moves from the class of a word $x$ to the class of $xa$, and whose accepting states are the classes of the words in $L$.
nodes.title: The Nerode automaton

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$. For every word $x \in \Sigma^*$, the word $x\varepsilon$ obtained by appending the empty word $\varepsilon$ is Nerode equivalent to $x$ for $L$.
nodes.title: Appending the empty word preserves the Nerode class

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$. If two words $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$, then for every word $z \in \Sigma^*$ the words $xz$ and $yz$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$.
nodes.title: Nerode equivalence is a right congruence

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$. If two words $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$, then for every symbol $a \in \Sigma$ the words $xa$ and $ya$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$.
nodes.title: Appending a symbol preserves Nerode equivalence

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA and let $L$ be the language it accepts. Two words $x$ and $y$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$ if and only if the states that $M$ reaches from its start state on reading $x$ and on reading $y$ are observationally equivalent, that is, $M$ accepts the same language from both states.
nodes.title: Nerode equivalence is equivalence of the reached states

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$. Two words $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$ if and only if, for every word $z \in \Sigma^*$, $xz \in L$ holds exactly when $yz \in L$.
nodes.title: Continuation characterization of Nerode equivalence

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA and let $L$ be the language it accepts. If $M$ reaches the same state from its start state on reading the words $x$ and $y$, then $x$ and $y$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$.
nodes.title: Words reaching the same DFA state are Nerode equivalent

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$. Two words $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ are Nerode equivalent for $L$ when they have the same left quotient, that is, $\{z \in \Sigma^* \mid xz \in L\} = \{z \in \Sigma^* \mid yz \in L\}$.
nodes.title: Nerode equivalence

nodes.summary: For a language $L$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$, the Nerode setoid of $L$ is the set $\Sigma^*$ of words equipped with Nerode equivalence for $L$, which is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
nodes.title: The Nerode setoid

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ and a state $q$ of $M$, let $L_q$ be the language of words $z$ such that running $M$ from $q$ on $z$ ends in an accepting state. The reachable residuals of $M$ form the set of the languages $L_q$ over all states $q$ that $M$ reaches from its start state on some input word.
nodes.title: Residual languages of reachable states

nodes.summary: A state is reachable when some input word reaches it from the start state.
nodes.title: Reachable state of a DFA

nodes.summary: For a language $L$ and a Nerode class $q$ of $L$, the representative of $q$ is a word whose Nerode class is $q$, chosen once and for all.
nodes.title: Representative of a Nerode class

nodes.summary: Two states $p$ and $q$ of a DFA $M$ are equivalent when they accept the same continuation language: for every word $z$, running $M$ from $p$ on $z$ ends in an accepting state if and only if running $M$ from $q$ on $z$ does.
nodes.title: Equivalent states of a DFA

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$ and $a \in \Sigma$ a symbol. Appending $a$ sends the Nerode class of a word $x$ to the Nerode class of $xa$; this is well defined because Nerode equivalence is preserved by appending a symbol.
nodes.title: Transition on Nerode classes

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA that accepts exactly the language $L$. Then the map sending each Nerode class of $L$ to the state that $M$ reaches from its start state on the chosen representative of the class is injective. In particular, $M$ has at least one distinct state for each Nerode class.
nodes.title: Distinct Nerode classes reach distinct states

nodes.summary: For a language $L$ and a DFA $M$ over the same alphabet, this map sends each Nerode class $q$ of $L$ to the state that $M$ reaches from its start state on the chosen representative of $q$.
nodes.title: Nerode classes to DFA states

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
